content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To learn how to play the violin, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Purchase a high-quality beginner violin (3 days)
Step 2. Memorize the names of the four strings (20 minutes)
Step 3. Apply rosin to the bow hair for the first time (10 minutes)
Step 4. Practice holding the bow with a relaxed grip (1 hour)
Step 5. Learn to read basic staff notation (2 days)
Step 6. Research local violin instructors (2 hours)
Step 7. Tighten the bow hair to the correct tension (1 minute)
Step 8. Learn how to use a digital tuner (15 minutes)
Step 9. Practice plucking open strings (30 minutes)
Step 10. Study the correct standing posture (45 minutes)
Step 11. Watch an instructional video on bridge placement (20 minutes)
Step 12. Buy a music stand (1 hour)
Step 13. Learn to sit properly while playing (30 minutes)
Step 14. Practice tuning the G string (5 minutes)
Step 15. Adjust the shoulder rest height (5 minutes)
Step 16. Play a clean G major scale (1 hour)
Step 17. Practice the "down-bow" motion (30 minutes)
Step 18. Read about violin maintenance and humidity (1 hour)
Step 19. Buy a soft cleaning cloth (15 minutes)
Step 20. Do finger stretching exercises (10 minutes)
Step 21. Learn the difference between a sharp and a flat (30 minutes)
Step 22. Practice the "up-bow" motion (30 minutes)
Step 23. Schedule an introductory lesson (15 minutes)
Step 24. Learn to identify the scroll and pegs (10 minutes)
Step 25. Play a simple folk melody (2 hours)
Step 26. Learn to keep the violin parallel to the floor (20 minutes)
Step 27. Memorize the treble clef notes (1 hour)
Step 28. Buy a metronome (20 minutes)
Step 29. Practice basic rhythm patterns (1 hour)
Step 30. Set up a dedicated practice space (2 hours)
Step 31. Watch a professional violin performance for inspiration (2 hours)
Step 32. Learn to play "Twinkle Twinkle Little Star" (3 hours)
Step 33. Practice placing the first finger on the E string (45 minutes)
Step 34. Learn to tuck the violin under the chin securely (15 minutes)
Step 35. Buy a book of beginner etudes (1 hour)
Step 36. Practice long, slow bow strokes (1 hour)
Step 37. Learn to play a basic slur (1 hour)
Step 38. Practice finding 'A' on the D string (30 minutes)
Step 39. Learn to use the pinky on the bow hand (45 minutes)
Step 40. Practice alternating between two notes (1 hour)
Step 41. Learn about the f-holes and soundpost (15 minutes)
Step 42. Attend a live symphony rehearsal (3 hours)
Step 43. Practice the second finger position (1 hour)
Step 44. Learn how to change a broken string (40 minutes)
Step 45. Perform a short piece for a friend (10 minutes)
Step 46. Research different types of violin strings (1 hour)
Step 47. Buy a comfortable chin rest (1 hour)
Step 48. Practice the third finger position (1 hour)
Step 49. Wipe down the strings after practice (5 minutes)
Step 50. Order a protective violin case (30 minutes)
Step 51. Learn about different violin wood types (2 hours)
Step 52. Watch a tutorial on vibrato basics (15 minutes)
Step 53. Listen to a recording of Paganini (10 minutes)
Step 54. Sign up for an online music theory course (30 minutes)
Step 55. Practice counting quarter notes (20 minutes)
Step 56. Learn how to open the violin case safely (2 minutes)
Step 57. Buy a cake of dark rosin (15 minutes)
Step 58. Read a biography of a famous violinist (4 hours)
Step 59. Practice identifying notes by ear (1 hour)
Step 60. Learn to use a mute for quiet practice (10 minutes)
Step 61. Practice dynamic changes from soft to loud (45 minutes)
Step 62. Do wrist flexibility drills (15 minutes)
Step 63. Choose a name for your violin (5 minutes)
Step 64. Visit a local luthier shop (2 hours)
Step 65. Clean the fingerboard of oil buildup (10 minutes)
Step 66. Practice the fourth finger (pinky) on the strings (1 hour)
Step 67. Learn to balance the violin without hands (10 minutes)
Step 68. Practice keeping the bow straight (1 hour)
Step 69. Learn a basic staccato stroke (45 minutes)
Step 70. Put a name tag on your violin case (5 minutes)
Step 71. Apply peg drops to stop slipping (10 minutes)
Step 72. Purchase a spare set of strings (20 minutes)
Step 73. Practice a simple duet with the teacher (30 minutes)
Step 74. Learn to store the bow properly (5 minutes)
Step 75. Learn the parts of the bow (frog, tip, hair) (15 minutes)
Step 76. Practice a one-octave D major scale (1 hour)
Step 77. Buy a humidifier for the case (15 minutes)
Step 78. Practice reading half notes and whole notes (30 minutes)
Step 79. Learn to use the fine tuners (10 minutes)
Step 80. Record your progress on video (15 minutes)
